about.title: Santa Barbara Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Santa Barbara is someone else's fault, the family is left carrying two burdens at once: grief, and a set of practical questions nobody wants to ask. Who can bring a claim? How long do we have? What does the law let us recover? California answers those questions through a civil wrongful death action, and it is a separate track from any criminal case the district attorney brings. Santa Barbara's public collision records for 2025 list 394 injury crashes, 518 people hurt, and 2 traffic deaths, with the highest counts along State Street, US-101, Cliff Drive and De La Vina Street. Each number represents a Santa Barbara County household changed overnight. Wrongful death claims here also arise outside of traffic: a fall on unsafe property, a defective product, a medical error. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects surviving family members with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Barbara Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you are connected with can tell you where your family fits before anything else moves forward.

items.title: The two-year clock is watched closely
items.desc: A California wrongful death claim generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting connected early keeps those deadlines from becoming a second loss.

items.title: Every category of loss is accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so pursuing these is not gated by upfront fees.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on US-101 or a city street in Santa Barbara. Does that change the deadline?
items.answer: It might. If a public agency such as Caltrans, the City of Santa Barbara, or Santa Barbara County is potentially responsible for a road condition or a government vehicle, California requires a formal claim with that agency on a much shorter timeline than the standard two years. An independent attorney can review the facts of the collision and tell you which deadlines apply to your situation.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate proceedings. A criminal case is brought by the prosecutor to punish the offense; it does not compensate your family for funeral costs, lost support, or the loss of companionship. A wrongful death action is the civil process that addresses those losses, and it can proceed regardless of how the criminal case ends.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect us with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service and is not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on a contingency basis, meaning there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. You are under no obligation after the initial conversation.
